title: Viva Feature Access Management (VFAM): who gets which Viva feature?
summary: The page passes: Microsoft's documentation supports the controls, policy precedence, limits, licensing prerequisite and corrected administrator roles. The open questions are appropriately limited to what the cited documentation does not state.

claims.claim: The feature access setting is reached through Settings > Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy > app > feature > Access setting.
claims.quote: select Viva from the settings menu. ... Select the Settings tab and select Manage feature access. ... Select Create a policy. ... select the app and feature ... Select the Access setting option

claims.claim: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy with ModuleId, FeatureId, Name, IsFeatureEnabled $false and Everyone disables the feature tenant-wide.
claims.quote: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId VivaInsights -FeatureId Reflection -Name DisableFeatureForAll -IsFeatureEnabled $false -Everyone

claims.claim: A policy audience is chosen through Settings > Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy > app > feature > Apply access settings to > Specific people and groups.
claims.quote: Select the Settings tab and select Manage feature access. ... Select Create a policy. ... select the app and feature ... Select Everyone or Specific people and groups under Apply access settings to.

claims.claim: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy with ModuleId, FeatureId, Name, IsFeatureEnabled $false, GroupIds and UserIds creates a policy disabling access for those groups and users.
claims.quote: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId VivaInsights -FeatureId Reflection -Name UsersAndGroups -IsFeatureEnabled $false -GroupIds group1@contoso.com,group2@contoso.com,57680382-61a5-4378-85ad-f72095d4e9c3 -UserIds user1@contoso.com,user2@contoso.com

claims.claim: The policy's user opt-out option is under Access setting after Settings > Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy > app > feature.
claims.quote: Name the policy and select the app and feature for which you'd like to set the policy. ... Select the Access setting option and choose On or Off to enable or disable the feature. Some features also allow the option for users to opt out.

claims.claim: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy with ModuleId, FeatureId, Name, IsFeatureEnabled $true and IsUserControlEnabled $true enables user opt-out.
claims.quote: The IsUserControlEnabled parameter specifies whether user control is enabled by the policy. Valid values are: ... $true: User control is enabled by the policy. Users can opt out of the feature.

claims.claim: An existing policy is edited through Settings > Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > More actions > Edit policy.
claims.quote: select Viva from the settings menu. ... Select the Settings tab and select Manage feature access. ... Select the vertical ellipses (More actions) and choose Edit policy.

claims.claim: Update-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy with ModuleId, FeatureId, PolicyId and GroupIds updates the existing policy's audience.
claims.quote: Update-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId VivaInsights -FeatureId Reflection -PolicyId xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx -GroupIds group1@contoso.com,group2@contoso.com

claims.claim: A policy is removed through Settings > Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > policy > Delete policy.
claims.quote: select Viva from the settings menu. ... Select the Settings tab and select Manage feature access. ... Select the policy you'd like to delete. ... Select Delete policy.

claims.claim: Remove-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy with ModuleId, FeatureId and PolicyId deletes the policy.
claims.quote: Remove-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId VivaInsights -FeatureId Reflection -PolicyId xxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx

claims.claim: The Agent Dashboard policy is reached through Settings > Microsoft Viva > Viva Insights > Set up and management > Access Management > Turn Advanced Insights on or off > Feature access management > Agent Dashboard > Add policy.
claims.quote: Under Access Management, select Turn Advanced Insights on or off. ... On the Feature access management page, select Agent Dashboard and Add policy.

claims.claim: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId VivaInsights -FeatureId AgentDashboard -Name <policy name> -IsFeatureEnabled $false -Everyone disables the Agent Dashboard tenant-wide.
claims.quote: Example: Turn off the Agent Dashboard for all users in your tenant ... ModuleId : VivaInsights ... FeatureId : AgentDashboard ... Name : DisableFeatureForAll ... IsFeatureEnabled : false ... Everyone

claims.claim: VFAM policies enable or disable specific Microsoft 365 and Viva features.
claims.quote: To control access to specific Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Viva features, you can create and update policies in the Microsoft 365 admin center or in PowerShell.

claims.claim: VFAM policies can enable or disable types of data processing.
claims.quote: You use policies to enable or disable specific features or types of data processing for users and groups in your tenant.

claims.where: summary; What it is: How it works
claims.claim: Policies can target the tenant, groups or individual users.
claims.quote: Policies are used to restrict or grant access to the specified feature for specific users, groups, or the entire tenant.

claims.claim: VFAM manages access to Insights features.
claims.quote: | Insights | Agent Dashboard | No | Global admin or AI admin | Viva Insights |

claims.claim: VFAM manages access to Pulse features.
claims.quote: | Pulse | Customization | No | Viva Pulse admin | Viva Pulse |

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: ModuleId identifies the module, with VivaInsights as the Insights module ID.
claims.quote: | Insights | VivaInsights |

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: VivaPulse is the Pulse module ID.
claims.quote: | Pulse | VivaPulse |

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: FeatureId identifies the feature within the module.
claims.quote: The FeatureId parameter specifies the feature in the Viva module that you want to add the policy for.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: A policy carries an enabled or disabled feature setting.
claims.quote: The IsFeatureEnabled parameter specifies whether or not the feature is enabled by the policy.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: One supported policy kind enables the feature for everyone in scope.
claims.quote: Enable the feature for everyone in the policy scope without considering user preference.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: One supported policy kind disables the feature for everyone in scope.
claims.quote: Disable the feature for everyone in the policy scope without considering user preference.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: One supported policy kind enables the feature while allowing users to opt out.
claims.quote: Enable the feature for everyone in the policy scope while providing users the ability to opt out.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: Soft disable opts everyone in scope out by default but allows users to opt in.
claims.quote: Enable the feature by opting out everyone in policy scope by default, while providing users the ability to opt in (soft disable).

claims.where: What it is: How it works; controls[2].note
claims.claim: The policy kinds and user controls are subject to feature support.
claims.quote: Admins can create the following policies, subject to feature support: ... Some features don't support opt-out user controls or soft disable policies for admins to activate.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 admin center and Exchange Online PowerShell manage the same access policies.
claims.quote: Policies can be created and managed by an admin who has permissions to do so in the Microsoft 365 admin center or by using PowerShell.

claims.where: What it is: How it works; Governance controls: Other surfaces
claims.claim: Copilot settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center also manage supported Copilot policies for Viva apps.
claims.quote: You can manage access to supported Copilot features in Viva apps that are available in your tenant.

claims.where: What it is: How it works; Governance controls: Other surfaces
claims.claim: Copilot policies remain in sync with policies managed through the feature access admin page.
claims.quote: You can manage Copilot policies through Copilot settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center. These policies remain in sync with policies managed through the admin page.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: Microsoft's feature table identifies each feature's module.
claims.quote: | App | Feature | Control for user opt-out? | Who can manage access | ModuleID |

claims.where: What it is: How it works; Governance controls: Roles; What to check
claims.claim: Microsoft's feature table identifies the role that manages each feature.
claims.quote: For more information, see the Who can manage access column in the following feature table.

claims.where: What it is: How it works; Why it matters
claims.claim: Microsoft's feature table identifies user opt-out support.
claims.quote: | App | Feature | Control for user opt-out? | Who can manage access | ModuleID |

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: Some features support only tenant-wide policies.
claims.quote: Some features only support policies that apply to the entire tenant, not specific users or groups.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: The settings apply to Agent 365 Business Analytics in Frontier preview where applicable.
claims.quote: The settings described below also apply to Agent 365 Business Analytics (Frontier preview) where applicable.

claims.where: What it is: Which policy wins
claims.claim: A user has one effective policy per feature.
claims.quote: A user has one effective policy for each feature.

claims.where: What it is: Which policy wins; Risks and limits: A narrower policy
claims.claim: User and group policies take priority over the tenant policy.
claims.quote: Policies assigned to a specific user or group take priority over the policy assigned to the entire tenant when determining whether a feature is enabled.

claims.where: What it is: Which policy wins
claims.claim: A policy assigned to a parent group reaches users in nested groups.
claims.quote: When users are in nested groups and you apply access policies to the parent group, the users in the nested groups receive the policies.

claims.where: What it is: Which policy wins
claims.claim: Nested groups and their users must be created in or synchronized to Microsoft Entra ID.
claims.quote: The nested groups and the users in those nested groups must be created in or synchronized to Microsoft Entra ID.

claims.where: What it is: Which policy wins
claims.claim: Without an individual or group policy, the organizational setting applies and may be the feature default.
claims.quote: If a user isn't assigned a policy as an individual or member of a group, the org-wide policy applies. It can be the default setting for the feature or a tenant-wide/org-wide policy created by the admin.

claims.where: What it is: Which policy wins
claims.claim: Within one scope level, the most restrictive enablement policy wins.
claims.quote: The most restrictive Policy Scope Level takes precedence first. Then within a single Policy Scope Level, the most restrictive Enablement Policy takes precedence.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: A narrower policy; What to check
claims.claim: A custom user or group policy can allow a feature whose organization-wide access is off.
claims.quote: if you have organization-wide access turned off, a custom policy could still allow access for specific users or groups.

claims.claim: Default states are feature-specific.
claims.quote: It can be the default setting for the feature or a tenant-wide/org-wide policy created by the admin.

claims.claim: The feature table does not list default states.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva feature access management feature table default state. Opened learn.microsoft.com/viva/feature-access-management; read the entire feature table: its columns cover app, feature, opt-out, managing role and module, not defaults.

claims.claim: The Viva Insights web app is on by default, so no policy change leaves that enablement default in place.
claims.quote: The Viva Insights web app is on by default.

claims.claim: The Agent Dashboard is on by default as part of the Viva Insights web app.
claims.quote: The Agent Dashboard is on by default as part of the Viva Insights web app.

claims.claim: Policy creation requires a supported version of Microsoft 365 or a Viva Suite license.
claims.quote: Policy creation requires the following elements: ... A supported version of Microsoft 365 or a Viva Suite license.

claims.claim: Microsoft links its Viva pricing page from the requirements.
claims.quote: A [supported version of Microsoft 365 or a Viva Suite license](https://www.microsoft.com/microsoft-viva/pricing).

claims.claim: The VFAM pages publish no separate policy creation or holding price or meter at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva Feature Access Management policy creation pricing meter charge. Read learn.microsoft.com/viva/feature-access-management, /viva/manage-access-policies and /viva/control-access-admin-center; they name license prerequisites but no policy price or meter.

claims.claim: An access policy cannot grant a feature that is otherwise unavailable to the tenant, with EDU as Microsoft's example.
claims.quote: if you have an EDU-based tenant, you can't use policies to gain access to features that aren't otherwise available to EDU tenants.

claims.where: controls[3].note; Risks and limits: Updates overwrite the audience
claims.claim: Specified UserIds, GroupIds or Everyone values overwrite the existing audience.
claims.quote: Values that you specify for the -UserIds and -GroupIds parameters or the -Everyone parameter overwrite any existing users or groups.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Updates overwrite the audience
claims.claim: When replacing the audience, omitting existing users or groups removes them from the policy.
claims.quote: Not including existing users or groups in the command effectively removes those specific users or groups from the policy.

claims.claim: Each feature permits at most 10 user/group policies.
claims.quote: You can assign a maximum of 10 policies per feature to users and groups.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risks and limits: Small limits
claims.claim: Each policy can cover at most 20 users and groups in total.
claims.quote: You can specify a maximum of 20 total users or groups (20 users and no groups, 10 users and 10 groups, etc.).

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risks and limits: Small limits
claims.claim: Each feature permits one additional tenant-wide policy using Everyone.
claims.quote: You can assign one additional policy per feature to the entire tenant by using the -Everyone parameter, which will function as a global default state for that feature across your organization.

claims.claim: Policy names must be unique.
claims.quote: Policy names must be unique.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Changes are not immediate
claims.claim: Access policy changes take effect within 24 hours unless the feature states otherwise.
claims.quote: Changes to access policies take effect for the user within 24 hours, unless noted for a specific feature.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Changes are not immediate
claims.claim: Copilot in Viva Engage access changes may take up to 48 hours.
claims.quote: Changes for Copilot in Viva Engage might take up to 48 hours.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Changes are not immediate
claims.claim: Group membership changes can take 24 hours to affect feature access.
claims.quote: When you add users or remove them from a Microsoft Entra ID or Microsoft 365 Group, it can take 24 hours before changes to their feature access take effect.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Opt-out choices reset
claims.claim: Fully enabling or disabling a feature resets the user's opt-in/out preference.
claims.quote: When an admin fully enables or disables a feature, the user's opt in/out preference resets to the default state.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Opt-out choices reset
claims.claim: Successive access changes less than 24 hours apart might not reset user preferences.
claims.quote: if there are multiple changes to access settings within a 24-hour period, the user's preference may not reset to the default state.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Deleted identities lose policies
claims.claim: Deleting user identities in Microsoft Entra ID deletes their VFAM user data.
claims.quote: When you delete user identities in Microsoft Entra ID, user data is also deleted from Viva feature access management.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Deleted identities lose policies
claims.claim: Users restored during the soft-deleted period need policies reassigned.
claims.quote: If user identities are re-enabled during the soft-deleted period, the admin needs to reassign policies to the user.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Deleted identities lose policies
claims.claim: Deleted Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft 365 groups are removed from stored policies.
claims.quote: When groups in Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft 365 are deleted, they're deleted from the stored policies.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Deleted identities lose policies
claims.claim: Groups restored during the soft-deleted period need policies reassigned.
claims.quote: If groups are re-enabled during the soft-deleted period, the admin needs to reassign policies to the groups.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Scope depends on the feature
claims.claim: Viva Insights web app auto-enablement supports tenant-level policies only.
claims.quote: This feature access control allows AI Administrators to enable or disable the auto-enablement feature for the Viva Insights web app in their tenant. This control supports tenant-level policies only, not user or group-level policies.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Scope depends on the feature
claims.claim: User and group policies have no effect on Viva Insights web app auto-enablement.
claims.quote: User- and group-level policies aren't supported for this feature and will not take effect if used.

claims.where: Risks and limits: One switch can cover an app
claims.claim: Disabling the Viva Insights web app disables the entire app, including the Copilot Dashboard.
claims.quote: Turning this control off disables the entire app, which includes the Microsoft Copilot Dashboard, Copilot Analytics reports, and advanced analysis and admin tools.

claims.where: Risks and limits: One switch can cover an app
claims.claim: Previous Copilot Dashboard access-control configurations now apply to the entire Viva Insights web app.
claims.quote: If you previously removed access to the Copilot Dashboard using Copilot Dashboard feature access management control or PowerShell, those configurations now apply to the entire Viva Insights web app.

claims.claim: The documented access controls are not available in GCC High.
claims.quote: The access controls described in this document aren't available in GCC-High or DoD.

claims.claim: The documented access controls are not available in DoD.
claims.quote: The access controls described in this document aren't available in GCC-High or DoD.

claims.claim: Microsoft directs GCC customers to the specific app's documentation for availability.
claims.quote: For GCC (Government Community Cloud), see the documentation for your specific app for availability.

claims.claim: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy requires Global Administrators membership or a role assigned at feature level.
claims.quote: Currently, you need to be a member of the Global Administrators role or the roles that have been assigned at the feature level to run this cmdlet.

claims.claim: Get-VivaModuleFeatureEnablement's reference requires Global Administrators membership.
claims.quote: Currently, you need to be a member of the Global Administrators role to run this cmdlet.

claims.claim: The Agent Dashboard can be managed by Global admin or AI admin.
claims.quote: | Insights | Agent Dashboard | No | Global admin or AI admin | Viva Insights |

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends least privilege and limiting use of Global Administrator.
claims.quote: Microsoft strongly advocates for the principle of least privilege. ... Global Administrator is a highly privileged role that you typically limit to emergency scenarios or when you can't use a different role.

claims.claim: The Viva Insights web app VFAM FeatureId is 'Viva Insights web app'.
claims.quote: ModuleId : VivaInsights ... FeatureId : Viva Insights web app

claims.where: Governance controls: Other surfaces; What to check
claims.claim: Get-VivaModuleFeature lists supported features and their IDs for a module.
claims.quote: Use the Get-VivaModuleFeature PowerShell cmdlet to get a list of all of the features available in a specific Microsoft 365 app and their associated IDs.

claims.where: controls[4].note; Governance controls: Other surfaces; What to check
claims.claim: Get-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy lists access policies and returns their policy IDs.
claims.quote: start by getting the specific UID for the access policy - you can get that by running Get-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy.

claims.claim: Get-VivaModuleFeatureEnablement returns a user's or group's feature enablement status.
claims.quote: Use the Get-VivaModuleFeatureEnablement cmdlet to view whether or not a feature in a Viva module is enabled for a specific user or group.

claims.claim: Microsoft points to VFAM change logs in Microsoft Purview for the history of policy creation, updates and deletions.
claims.quote: For a history of policy creation, updates, and deletions, see the Viva Feature Access Management (VFAM) change logs for your organization in Microsoft Purview.

claims.claim: VFAM requires Exchange Online PowerShell 3.2.0 or later when managed through PowerShell.
claims.quote: Access to Exchange Online PowerShell Version 3.2.0 or later.

claims.claim: Non-mail-enabled groups require Exchange PowerShell 3.5.1 or later.
claims.quote: If you need to use non-mail-enabled groups you must have access to Exchange PowerShell version 3.5.1 or later.

claims.claim: The VFAM guide specifies Exchange PowerShell 3.8.0 or later for soft disable.
claims.quote: If you need to setup policies with the user opted-out by default (soft-disable), you must have access to Exchange PowerShell version 3.8.0 or later.

claims.claim: The Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy reference specifies 3.8.0-Preview2 or later for IsUserOptedInByDefault.
claims.quote: ### -IsUserOptedInByDefault ... Note: This parameter is available in module version 3.8.0-Preview2 or later.

claims.claim: Soft disable adds IsUserOptedInByDefault $false to an enabled feature policy with user controls.
claims.quote: The policy enables the feature for the specified users, allows user controls, and opted out users by default (Soft Disable policy).

claims.claim: IsUserOptedInByDefault requires IsUserControlEnabled $true.
claims.quote: This parameter can be set only when the IsUserControlEnabled parameter is set to $true.

claims.claim: Everyone must not be combined with GroupIds or UserIds.
claims.quote: Don't use this switch with the GroupIds or UserIds parameters.

claims.claim: The Agent Dashboard is a public preview.
claims.quote: The Agent Dashboard is for public preview customers only.

claims.claim: The AI admin manages Agent Dashboard enablement.
claims.quote: The AI admin can enable or disable the Agent Dashboard at the tenant, group, or user level using the Agent Dashboard VFAM control in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Agent Dashboard enablement policies support tenant, group and user scope.
claims.quote: The AI admin can enable or disable the Agent Dashboard at the tenant, group, or user level using the Agent Dashboard VFAM control in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Access to the Agent Dashboard requires both its VFAM control and the Viva Insights web app control to be enabled.
claims.quote: To access the Agent Dashboard, both the Viva Insights web app control and this control must be enabled.

claims.claim: A Learn search finds no Graph or REST API for managing VFAM policies.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva Feature Access Management VFAM Microsoft Graph REST API policies; site:learn.microsoft.com/graph Viva feature policy. Read the three VFAM guides and Graph vfamBasePolicyAuditRecord; the latter is an audit resource for network filtering, not policy management.

claims.claim: The VFAM pages point to change logs without naming audit operations.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva Feature Access Management Microsoft Purview audit activities operation names; VFAM audit operation. Read the three VFAM guides and Purview audit-log-activities excerpts; the guides direct readers to change logs without naming events.

claims.claim: The admin-center VFAM page does not mention soft disable.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva admin center soft disable IsUserOptedInByDefault. Read learn.microsoft.com/viva/control-access-admin-center in full; it documents on, off and opt-out, but does not mention soft disable.
